method_notes: Targeted gap-closing pass on the Scottish NON-SPORT >=1,000 estate, run against the 148 Scottish records already in venues.json (89 football stadiums, 12 rugby, 5 cricket, 5 racecourses, 2 motorsport, 1 other sport = 114 sport; 34 non-sport). All existing Scottish canonical_name+city pairs and alternative_names were extracted programmatically from venues.json before research and used as the de-duplication key set (231 keys). POPULATIONS WORKED THROUGH: (1) Operator portfolios - Capital Theatres (Festival Theatre, King's, The Studio), ATG (Edinburgh Playhouse), Academy Music Group (O2 Academy Glasgow, O2 Academy Edinburgh = Corn Exchange, O2 ABC Glasgow), AEG (Edinburgh Park Arena), ASM Global (P&J Live), Glasgow Life (full venue-hire estate enumerated from https://www.glasgowlife.org.uk/venue-hire), Aberdeen Performing Arts, Horsecross Arts (Perth), Eden Court, Dundee Rep, OnFife, Culture NL, South Lanarkshire Leisure & Culture, East Ayrshire Leisure, OneRen, Inverclyde Leisure, Live Active Leisure. (2) Council venue estates - Glasgow, Edinburgh, Aberdeen, Dundee, Stirling, Perth & Kinross, Highland, Fife, Falkirk, North and South Lanarkshire, Renfrewshire, Inverclyde, East/South Ayrshire, Dumfries & Galloway, Moray, Orkney. (3) Convention bureaux - Convention Edinburgh / Meeting Edinburgh (driven in a real browser: its venue search exposes a minRoomCapacity + roomConfiguration filter and returned EXACTLY 7 Edinburgh venues with a single room of >=1,000 theatre-style, which is the single most useful negative result in this pass); Glasgow Convention Bureau (visitglasgow.org.uk, capacity>=1000 filter returned 9 venues, all of which proved to be whole-venue totals, not >=1,000 single rooms); VisitScotland Business Events. (4) Royal Highland & Agricultural Society showground estate. (5) Scottish university venue estates - Glasgow, Edinburgh, Strathclyde, St Andrews, Aberdeen, Heriot-Watt, Dundee. (6) Major arts organisations and festival operators (Edinburgh International Festival, Assembly Festival, Edinburgh Festival Fringe, DF Concerts, Royal Edinburgh Military Tattoo). JUDGEMENT ON THE TRUE SCOTTISH ESTATE: the previous pass's instinct was broadly right but it stopped ~20 venues short. Scotland's genuine non-sport >=1,000 estate is small by English standards and is overwhelmingly concentrated in Glasgow and Edinburgh, but it is materially larger than 17 theatres/concert halls + 2 conference venues. The additions here fall into five families the earlier passes missed entirely: (a) large-capacity non-theatre music venues (SWG3 Galvanizers 1,250); (b) OUTDOOR council-run major event venues, which are among the biggest audiences in Scotland and had zero representation - Glasgow Green (TRNSMT, 50,000/day), Bellahouston Park (35,000), Slessor Gardens Dundee (12,000 approved), Edinburgh Castle Esplanade (8,800), Ross Bandstand (2,500), Kelvingrove Bandstand (2,200); (c) ceremonial/university and independent-school auditoria at 1,000-1,150 (Bute Hall 1,100, Assembly Hall 1,100, George Watson's Assembly Hall 1,040) - a family the census had touched only via McEwan Hall; (d) the closed/demolished estate that a census must still carry (AECC 8,500, O2 ABC 1,300, Motherwell Concert Hall, Grand Hall Kilmarnock closed to 2028); (e) the pipeline (Edinburgh Arena 8,500, Dunard Centre 1,000). Outside the central belt the >=1,000 estate is genuinely thin and I evidenced that rather than assumed it: Inverness tops out at Eden Court's 840-850 seat Empire Theatre; Fife's only >=1,000 house is the Alhambra Dunfermline (1,232 seated / 2,100 standing) with Rothes Halls at 596 and Adam Smith at 475; Ayrshire's Grand Hall main hall is 900 seated and currently closed; Moray, the Borders, Argyll and the Western Isles have nothing at >=1,000; Orkney's Pickaquoy Centre (1,600) is the only island venue at scale. Non-sport >=1,000 conference/exhibition capacity in Scotland is confirmed to be just six sites: SEC, EICC, P&J Live, Royal Highland Centre, Macdonald Aviemore Resort (Osprey Arena 1,150) and Easterbrook Hall Dumfries (1,000) - every other Scottish academic/hotel/unique venue checked topped out below 1,000 in a single room (Strathclyde TIC 450, Heriot-Watt James Watt Centre 465, Aberdeen Elphinstone Hall 400, St Andrews Younger Hall 958, Dundee Bonar Hall 476, Glasgow Burrell 300, Riverside 800 whole-museum, Engine Works 650, Kelvingrove Art Gallery Centre Hall 600, Mitchell Complex 90). SCOPE BOUNDARY TAKEN: outdoor urban event spaces with a regular, promoted, ticketed major-event programme (Glasgow Green, Bellahouston, Slessor Gardens, the two bandstands, the Castle Esplanade) are included; private-estate one-weekend festival sites (Strathallan Castle, Belladrum, Balado) are NOT, and neither are sport venues. Two hotel/resort records (Macdonald Aviemore, Prestonfield) are included only because each has an evidenced >=1,000 SINGLE-ROOM event space; no hotel was admitted on a whole-property total. One record re-lists an existing census venue (Royal Highland Centre, Edinburgh) with the exact same canonical_name and city purely to attach first-party hall-level capacities and the verified postcode. NOTHING here activates a source; no registry, sources/*.json, venues/*.json or data/* file was read for write or modified.

venues.scale_description: North Lanarkshire's principal concert and theatre complex, part of Motherwell Civic Centre and owned by North Lanarkshire Council. Theatres Trust records a 400-seat theatre with an adjacent public hall (the Concert Hall) 'accommodating over 1,000 people', placing the concert hall above the 1,000 threshold for this census even though no exact figure is published. Closed with immediate effect on 12 September 2023 after reinforced autoclaved aerated concrete (RAAC) was found in a deteriorated condition - water ingress, exposed reinforcement, compromised structural performance - assessed as a high-to-critical structural risk and ultimately found in 95% of the roof area. Repair was costed at over £10m and judged economically unviable; demolition was approved, planning and listed building consent applications were submitted in 2025 and a further application in May 2026, with a replacement planned at Ravenscraig. The Culture NL events team relocated to Airdrie Town Hall (515 seated / 650 standing plus 83 balcony), which is itself below the census threshold.
